To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NMDA induces two distinct types of repetitive burst discharges in the same magnocellular hypothalamic neurons.
NMDA can induce rhythmic bursting activity in a majority of hypothalamic magnocelluar neurons, and that this activity is resistant to tetrodoxotin and to blockers of L‐ and T‐type Ca2+ currents.

NMDA receptors can mediate two types of repetitive bursting activities, which differ in their dependence on voltage‐gated Ca2+ channels and Ca2+‐activated K+ channels, in hypothalamic magnocelluar neurons in vitro.

the effects of NMDA receptor stimulation on the activity of neurons of the guinea‐pig hypothalamic magnocelluar nucleus (MNC).
the study of the mechanisms of the rhythmic burst firing of neurons in the hypothalamic magnocelluar dorsal nucleus.
the effects of NMDA on the activity of hypothalamic magnocelluar nucleus neurons in vitro
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NMDA receptor is not only involved in the induction of bursting activity but also in the modulation of the frequency of the bursts.

NMDA‐dependent rhythmic bursting activity is mediated by a voltage‐dependent Ca2+ influx through NMDA receptor‐operated channels, and that it is sustained by the activation of Ca2+‐independent K+ conductances.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMDA receptors in the hypothalamus may play an important role in generating endogenous rhythmic bursting activity.
the NMDA receptor can mediate two distinct types of repetitive firing activity, depending on the level of depolarization and the presence of Ca2+‐activated K+currents.

the rhythmic burst activity in dorsal nucleus magnocellular neurons in vitro is not due to the activation of a Ca2+‐activated non‐specific cation conductance, but to the activation of NMDARs, which is voltage dependent and involves the opening of apamin‐sensitive Ca‐dependent K+channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glutamate can induce two different types of rhythmic activity, depending on the strength and/or the pattern of glutamatergics drive.
NMDA receptors can mediate two distinct rhythmic bursting behaviours, depending on the strength and duration of their activation.
